Friedrich Leopold, Graf zu Stolberg (1750-1819), was a German poet, and this 1911 Britannica entry follows his life and his change of faith. He was born at Bramstedt in Holstein, a younger son of Count Christian Stolberg. He studied at Göttingen and stood out in the famous poets' circle called the Hain.

In 1777 he became envoy of the prince bishop of Lübeck at Copenhagen, though he often stayed at Eutin with his friend Voss. He married Agnes von Witzleben in 1782 and sang her in his poems. After her early death he served as Danish envoy at Berlin and married again. In 1791 he took a court post at Eutin, but in 1800 he retired to Münster. There he joined the Roman Catholic Church, a step his old friend Voss attacked with force.
